newsitem.title: USA: Ford first-quarter profits more than double.
newsitem.headline: Ford first-quarter profits more than double.

text.p: Ford Motor Co., reaping the rewards of lower costs and high-margin products, on Wednesday posted first-quarter earnings of $1.47 billion, more than double the $653 million it made a year ago.
On a per-share basis, Ford reported fully diluted earnings of $1.20, beating the Wall Street consensus estimate of about 90 cents. A year ago, Ford had fully diluted earnings of 53 cents.
Profits from Ford's U.S. automotive operations, which contribute about two-thirds of its total automotive revenue, soared to $836 million from $48 million a year ago.
"The changes we have been making to our automotive operations for the past two years are beginning to pay off," Ford Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Alex Trotman said in a statement.

Ford's first-quarter profits from worldwide automotive operations were also up sharply, to $1 billion from $142 million a year ago, thanks to smaller losses in South America and a profit rebound in Europe. Total revenues rose to $36.2 billion from $35.2 billion.
Ford's year-ago results were hampered by a number of high-volume product launches, both in the United States and Europe, such as a new Ford Fiesta small car and a redesigned F-Series pickup truck.

Ford's Financial Services Group's first-quarter earnings fell to $465 million from a record $511 million a year ago. The company attributed the drop to last year's sale of most of the assets of its USL Capital unit.

But increased credit losses also took a toll in the 1997 first period on Ford Credit, the largest part of the Financial Services unit. Ford Credit earned $276 million in the first quarter, down from $339 million a year ago.
Ford's stock gained 37.5 cents to $33.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
